summary: Cross-tenant model pin leak observed after auth token rotation during canary promote
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of requests from Acme Health began receiving responses generated by a different tenant's pinned model immediately after an auth token rotation event that coincided with a canary promote in us-east. The symptom is cross-tenant 'pinned-model' leakage: tenant A (Acme Health) traffic was intermittently routed to tenant B's pinned variant for short windows (~5-30s).

Impact:
- Customer-visible incorrect outputs (safety/PHI risk for Acme Health).
- ~0.5% of requests during the window returned wrong model outputs; spike lasted ~18 minutes across rolling canary.
- Service remained up (no 5xx), but correctness SLO breached for affected tenant.

Environment:
- Production (prod us-east primary, some failover to eu-west).
- Edge proxy version: edge-proxy@v3.14.2.
- Orchestrator: orchestrator@1.9.0 (canary promote triggered at ~2026-03-10T16:02:00Z).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Scheduled canary promote originated from control plane at 2026-03-10T16:02:00Z.
2) Around the same time control plane triggered a tenant auth token rotation for an unrelated customer cohort (rotation propagation ~16:02:05Z).
3) Edge proxy logs show a short-lived persistence of an X-Tenant-Pin header in the upstream cache when a connection pool was reused during handshake renegotiation.
4) Reused connection returned variant responses where the pinned model id in response metadata mismatched the request tenant id.

Observed behavior:
- Header-stored pin metadata persisted across pooled connections in edge-proxy when TLS session renegotiation + auth refresh occurred.
- Orchestrator rollouts and canary weight adjustments exacerbated transient routing decisions, causing some requests to be stamped with wrong pin context and routed to the pinned instance for the other tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Pin metadata must be isolated per-tenant and cleared on any auth header change or session renegotiation; no cross-tenant leakage should occur.

Relevant logs/traces/metrics:
- edge-proxy access logs: correlation_id log lines showing tenant_id mismatch and pin_id mismatch (attached snippets).
- Tracing: spike in routing decisions to variant B for tenant A between 2026-03-10T16:02:07Z and 2026-03-10T16:20:30Z.
- Dashboard: per-tenant correctness alerts fired for Acme Health.

Workaround in place:
- Temporary mitigation: we rolled edge-proxy pool mode to 'no-keepalive' for Acme Health's edge pool to force fresh connections (applied 16:25Z) — this reduced cross-tenant responses to near zero.
- Control plane paused canary weight adjustments to avoid further routing noise.

Business impact and risk:
- High: Acme Health processes PHI-related prompts; incorrect model outputs are not acceptable and require immediate remediation and root cause analysis.

First response due at: 2026-03-11 (SLA).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: connection-pool reuse combined with header-caching leads to stale pin header persisting across tenant requests when an auth rotation occurs mid-handshake.

What we verified so far:
- Reproduced header persistence in a dev harness with edge-proxy v3.14.2 when TLS session resumption and auth refresh occur quickly on pooled connections.
- Orchestrator logs show canary promote triggered route updates that read pins from the control plane snapshot; some edge nodes had inconsistent snapshots for ~10s.
- Cache TTL for pin metadata in edge-proxy was 60s; combined with the pool reuse this allowed an incorrect pin to be served for short windows.

Hypotheses to validate next:
1) Edge-proxy should invalidate cached pin metadata on auth header change or on detecting tenant_id mismatch in handshake; currently it only invalidates on explicit cache expiry.
2) Connection pool tagging by tenant was insufficiently strict and allowed cross-tenant lease reuse under high churn.

Telemetry/Artefacts collected:
- Access log snippets (ids redacted) and trace IDs: trace-20260310-001..007.
- Heap/metrics snapshots from edge-proxy host-12 during incident.
- Orchestrator snapshot diffs between control plane publishes at 16:02:00Z and 16:02:10Z.

resolution: In progress: hotfix (edge-proxy v3.14.3) deployed to production; it includes two mitigations: 1) pin cache invalidation when auth headers or tenant id changes, and 2) stronger tenant tagging of connection pools to prevent cross-tenant reuse. Post-deploy monitoring for 48h required. If stable, will mark Resolved and schedule follow-up security review.
workaround: Applied 'no-keepalive' on Acme Health's edge pool (temporary) and paused canary weight adjustments until edge-proxy patch was available. These actions mitigated the leakage while hotfix was prepared.
next_steps: Run a focused penetration/regression test for pin isolation across tenants with high churn and auth rotations.
Backfill control plane snapshot consistency checks to reduce 10s snapshot divergence during publishes.
Prepare post-incident security review and customer-facing incident report for Acme Health (privacy-focused summary).
